def: Every expression belongs to exactly one of lvalue, xvalue, prvalue; this static property is called its value category. Together with the type it determines reference binding, overload resolution, and the result of `decltype`.
An expression whose evaluation determines the identity of an object, function, non-static data member, or direct base class relationship; i.e. the collective name for lvalues and xvalues.

An expression whose evaluation initializes an object (its result object) or computes the value of an operand of an operator, or an expression of type cv `void`. Since C++17 a prvalue is not itself an object.
A glvalue that denotes an object whose resources can be reused, e.g. `std::move(x)`, a call to a function returning `T&&`, or a member of a materialized temporary.
A glvalue that is not an xvalue. Variable names (including variables of rvalue reference type), `*p`, `++i`, and string literals are all lvalues.
A prvalue or an xvalue; an expression that can bind to an rvalue reference.

The object initialized by a prvalue, provided by the context in which the prvalue appears (a variable, return value, parameter, or materialized temporary). A prvalue of cv `void` has no result object.

The standard conversion of a prvalue of type `T` to an xvalue: the prvalue is evaluated with a newly created temporary object as its result object. Requires `T` to be complete, and for class types requires the destructor to be usable.

An object with dynamic type Tobj is type-accessible through a glvalue of type Tref if and only if Tref is similar to Tobj, to the signed/unsigned type corresponding to Tobj, or to one of `char`/`unsigned char`/`std::byte`. Reading or writing an object through a glvalue through which it is not type-accessible is UB (the strict aliasing rule).
An lvalue whose type is neither const-qualified nor a function type. Built-in assignment, increment, and decrement require a modifiable lvalue.

The common type to which two pointer (or pointer-to-member, `std::nullptr_t`) operands are uniformly converted, used by `==`, `<`, `<=>`, `?:`, etc.; determined in order by null pointer constants, `void*`, noexcept, base/derived, and similar types.

An operand that is not evaluated, such as the operand of `sizeof`, `decltype`, `noexcept`, or non-polymorphic `typeid`. Names in it do not constitute odr-uses, but semantic checking proceeds as usual.

An expression evaluated only for its side effects, with its result discarded, such as an expression statement, the left operand of a comma, or `(void)e`. The lvalue-to-rvalue conversion is applied only to volatile glvalues of particular forms; prvalues of object type are materialized.

A sequence of standard conversions in a fixed order: at most one lvalue transformation (lvalue-to-rvalue/array-to-pointer/function-to-pointer), at most one promotion or conversion, at most one function pointer conversion, and at most one qualification conversion.

An expression `E` in an `if` condition, `!`, `&&`, etc. is converted to `bool` if and only if `bool t(E);` is well-formed; because this is direct-initialization, `explicit` conversion functions are considered.

The standard conversion of a glvalue of non-function, non-array type to a prvalue, which in essence reads the object's value; for non-class types cv is removed, while for class types the result object is copy-initialized.
Two types are similar if they are the same after erasing the cv-qualifiers at every level (and allowing array bounds to differ between known and unknown). E.g. `int**` and `const int* const*`.

The type obtained from two similar types by taking the union of cv-qualifiers at each level (and unknown array bounds), then adding `const` to every intermediate level outside any level that changed; `T1` can be qualification-converted to `T2` if and only if their qualification-combined type is `T2`.

The standard conversion of integers of rank lower than `int`, bit-fields, character types, `bool`, and unscoped enumerations to `int` (or `unsigned int`, etc.); in overload resolution it ranks as a "promotion", better than an ordinary conversion.
An integer literal with value zero, or a prvalue of type `std::nullptr_t`. `'\0'`, `false`, and const variables with value 0 are not.

The algorithm by which binary arithmetic, comparison, bitwise operators, and `?:` bring two arithmetic or enumeration operands to a common type; for integers, each is first integrally promoted, then they are merged by signedness and rank.

A unary `+`/`-`, additive, or multiplicative expression all of whose operands are of arithmetic type. If its mathematical result is neither within the range of representable values of its type nor ±∞ or NaN of that type, the behavior is undefined.
